# Video {.unnumbered}

## Overview

Video extends images with a temporal dimension, turning visual understanding into a spatiotemporal problem. This section covers the full stack across five chapters: representing and measuring motion and the discriminative architectures built on top of it, vision-language models that understand, retrieve, and reason over video, the structural task of splitting video into shots and scenes, the benchmark landscape used to evaluate all of it, and generative models that synthesize temporally coherent clips.

**Chapter Scope**:

- **Video Fundamentals: Motion and Spatiotemporal Architectures** (Chapter 10): Video as a spatiotemporal signal, optical flow (classical and learned), 3D CNNs (C3D, I3D, R(2+1)D, SlowFast), video transformers (TimeSformer, Video Swin, ViViT), and self-supervised pretraining (VideoMAE, V-JEPA)
- **Video Understanding** (Chapter 11): Downstream video tasks (action recognition, temporal grounding, VQA, retrieval, tracking), vision-language model architectures from Q-Former to M-RoPE, the Qwen-VL evolution, specialized and contrastive video VLMs, and the two-stage retrieval-and-reranking pipeline
- **Video Temporal Segmentation** (Chapter 12): Shot boundary detection and scene boundary detection as the two-stage pipeline that turns raw frames into searchable, retrieval-ready units — classical signals, learned detectors, and Scene-VLM-style sequence labelling
- **Video Understanding Benchmarks** (Chapter 13): A systematic tour of the benchmark landscape — action recognition, long-video, VQA/reasoning, temporal grounding, captioning/retrieval, and egocentric benchmarks, plus practical guidance for choosing one
- **Video Generation** (Chapter 14): Diffusion fundamentals for video (3D-VAE compression, DiT vs. U-Net), training-from-scratch (VDM, Imagen Video, Sora, CogVideoX), fine-tuning image models (Make-A-Video, Video LDM), training-free adaptation (Text2Video-Zero), autoregressive video generation, and evaluation (FVD, VBench)

**Interview Relevance**: Video understanding and generation are central to roles at Meta (Reels ranking, Movie Gen), Google DeepMind (Gemini, Veo, Genie), OpenAI (Sora), Tesla and Waymo (temporal scene understanding), and TikTok/YouTube (recommendation, search, and moderation at scale). Expect questions on extending image architectures to video efficiently, token-budget trade-offs for long-context video LLMs, how modern video generators (Sora, CogVideoX) differ architecturally from image diffusion models, how a video is split into shots/scenes for retrieval, and how to evaluate video understanding or generation quality.

**Prerequisites**: Part II (CNNs, Vision Transformers), Part III (Self-Supervised Learning), Part IV (Diffusion Models), and the Foundation Models for Segmentation chapter (§sec-segmentation). Familiarity with 2D convolution, multi-head self-attention, rotary positional embeddings, and the DDPM training objective.
